the theory of the stability of the equilibrium of a system is a theory of the motion of a system in a neighborhood of its equilibrium.

the theory of the stability of a system of particles interacting according to the law of forces of the type of Newtonian attraction, repulsion, and repulsion-atraction, has been developed in a complete and final form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Kelvin problem, in which we are interested, is solved for a wide class of force functions.
the problem of instability of a system of particles in a force field is reduced to the problem of stability of the equilibrium of the same system in an auxiliary force field.
the instability of equilibrium of the system of interacting particles in a bounded volume of the Euclidean space is a consequence of the instability of equilibrium in an infinite space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kelvin problem is a special case of the instability of equilibrium in the presence of a subharmonic potential.
the instability of a system of particles in a bounded volume is a general phenomenon and not a peculiarity of a special system.
the stability of the equilibrium of the system of interacting particles can only be guaranteed if the force function is subharmonic.
